metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: While we have focused on population-genetic applications of diffusion processes, this approach is also very useful for solving a number of problems in quantitative genetics. When attention shifts from individual alleles to a quantitative character, diffusions typically follow mean phenotypes instead of allele frequencies. Two well-studied diffusions, Brownian motion and the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, are especially useful (Chapter 12).
